_comment: The full spec/target-spec.md §PVT grid for the closed-loop vref bench: 5 process labels x 3 supplies x 3 temperatures = 45 points. Run by run-grid.sh on the Spot batch fleet (issue #30); narrowed to typ/27 C/3.30 V by run.sh for a single-corner local probe.
PORTABLE BY CONSTRUCTION (issue #30). Nothing in this file is a path that exists only on the submitting host, so the same request serves `--backend local` and `--backend batch`:

- `models.pdk` selects the variant and the fleet's batch image (klayout-tools#2727 publishes sg13cmos5l); each corner's sections name their own PDK-relative library, so no `models.lib` and no generated corner bundle is needed. An absolute host path here is refused on batch (`models_lib_host_path`).

- `options.stage_model_inputs` ships THIS host's pinned model libraries and their whole `.include`/`.lib` closure with the job, so the models that ran are bound by sha256 to sim/pdk.json's pinned revision (`environment.staged_model_inputs` and `remote.runner_model_inputs` both list them) rather than being whatever the fleet image carries. The image's own SG13CMOS5L tree publishes no readable revision stamp (`worker_environment.pdk.stamp_text` is null), so without staging the grid could not be bound to the pin at all -- see README.md 'What the fleet runner cannot prove'. On `--backend local` the option is accepted and does nothing.

- `options.osdi_preload` entries are written as literal `$PDK_ROOT/...`, so they are runner-resolved off-host and expanded from the environment locally. They are NOT staged, so the OSDI objects that load are the executing host's own.

- `netlist` is the deck run-grid.sh/run.sh generate under sim/build/ (gitignored); its `.include` of the migrated DUT is staged with the job by klt's include-closure staging. The runner substitutes an absolute path; the relative default below is what the generated deck's location is, so `klt sim --dry-run` works straight from the repo root after a runner has written it.
Process labels map to model sections exactly as the §PVT table does: pnpMPA has no skew section, so sf and fs read cornerPNP/cornerRES `typ`.

`netlist_source` is `schematic`: the DUT is the xschem-exported netlist migrated by decision record 0006, NOT an extracted one. (It read `extracted` before issue #30 -- a provenance mislabel; see README.md 'The netlist_source correction'.)

LIMITS. Only the settle criterion is graded. The 'Output reference, nominal' row's ratified target is 'nominal at the TC-null point' -- a method, not a number -- so no numeric accuracy bound exists to copy here, and inventing one would be ratifying a number (CLAUDE.md). What IS graded at all 45 points is the criterion decision record 0009 already ratified for this bench: the closed loop settles. vref_v itself is recorded as evidence at every point, with a plausible_range that catches a converged-but-degenerate solution instead of letting it be recorded as a reference.
